draft.title: Levers
card: A lever is a rigid bar that turns about a fixed point called the fulcrum. The effort is the force you apply. The load is the force the lever works against.
the fulcrum is between the effort and the load, as in a seesaw.
the load is between the fulcrum and the effort, as in a wheelbarrow.
the effort is between the fulcrum and the load, as in tweezers.
draft.remember: The class of a lever depends on which of the three parts sits in the middle.

a.q: A nutcracker has its hinge at one end, the nut in the middle and your hand at the other end. Which part is in the middle?
opts: The load, so it is a second class lever
The fulcrum, so it is a first class lever
The effort, so it is a third class lever
The load, so it is a first class lever
a.why: The hinge is the fulcrum, your hand gives the effort, and the nut is the load. The load sits between the fulcrum and the effort, so it is second class. Calling it first class would need the fulcrum in the middle.
a.clue: Find the fulcrum and the effort first. Which part is left in the middle?

b.q: Sam uses a garden spade to lift a rock. The spade rests on a brick, Sam pushes down on the handle end, and the rock is under the blade end. The brick is between Sam's hands and the rock. What class of lever is this?
opts: First class, because the fulcrum is in the middle
Second class, because the fulcrum is in the middle
First class, because the effort is in the middle
Third class, because the load is in the middle
b.why: The brick is the fulcrum, and it sits between the effort at the handle and the load under the blade. A fulcrum in the middle makes a first class lever, like a seesaw. Second class needs the load in the middle, and here the load is at the end.
b.clue: Name the part that sits between the other two.

wants.brief: Three side-by-side labelled bar diagrams of levers. First class: a seesaw with the fulcrum in the middle, effort at one end and load at the other. Second class: a wheelbarrow with the load in the middle, the fulcrum (wheel) at one end and effort (handles) at the other. Third class: tweezers with the effort in the middle, the fulcrum at one end and the load at the other. Label Fulcrum, Effort and Load on each.
wants.why: Seeing where the three parts sit makes the three classes easy to tell apart.

a.best: The load, so it is a second class lever

b.best: First class, because the fulcrum is in the middle
